title: What happens to six when we divide it?
description: Six is divided by three and by one quarter, and each answer is compared with six. A divisor above one gives a smaller answer and a divisor between zero and one gives a greater one. Keeko raises the doubt that dividing always makes a number smaller.
teaching_notes: One idea: dividing by a number above one gives a quotient less than the dividend, and dividing by a number between zero and one gives a greater quotient. Watch for students who believe dividing always makes a number smaller.

source: Find 6 ÷ 3 and 6 ÷ (1/4) and compare each quotient with the

video_script.wrong_move: expects every division to give a quotient less than the dividend
video_script.payoff_line: Two is less than six, and twenty four is greater than six

final_answer.value: 2 is less than 6; 24 is greater than 6
final_answer.spoken: two is less than six, and twenty four is greater than six
